## Proof

We seek all $A \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ such that for every $B \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$:
$$\xi(A, B) = n\,\mathrm{tr}(AB) - \mathrm{tr}(A)\,\mathrm{tr}(B) = 0.$$

**Key observation.** Since $\mathrm{tr}(B) = \mathrm{tr}(IB)$, we have
$$\mathrm{tr}(A)\,\mathrm{tr}(B) = \mathrm{tr}(A)\cdot\mathrm{tr}(IB) = \mathrm{tr}\!\big(\mathrm{tr}(A)\cdot I \cdot B\big).$$

Therefore
$$\xi(A,B) = n\,\mathrm{tr}(AB) - \mathrm{tr}\!\big(\mathrm{tr}(A)\,I\,B\big) = \mathrm{tr}\!\Big(\big(nA - \mathrm{tr}(A)\,I\big)\,B\Big).$$

**Using non-degeneracy of the trace form.** The bilinear form $(C, B) \mapsto \mathrm{tr}(CB)$ on $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ is non-degenerate: if $\mathrm{tr}(CB) = 0$ for all $B$, then $C = 0$. (This follows, for instance, by testing against $B = E_{ji}$, which extracts the $(i,j)$-entry of $C$.)

Applying this with $C = nA - \mathrm{tr}(A)\,I$:

$$\xi(A, B) = 0 \;\;\forall B \in M_n(\mathbb{C}) \iff nA - \mathrm{tr}(A)\,I = 0 \iff A = \frac{\mathrm{tr}(A)}{n}\,I.$$

**Characterizing the solutions.** The condition $A = \frac{\mathrm{tr}(A)}{n}\,I$ says precisely that $A$ is a scalar multiple of the identity matrix. Setting $A = \lambda I$ with $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, we check: $\mathrm{tr}(A) = n\lambda$, so $\frac{\mathrm{tr}(A)}{n}I = \lambda I = A$. ✓

Conversely, every scalar multiple $\lambda I$ satisfies the condition. Hence
$$U_\perp = \{\lambda I : \lambda \in \mathbb{C}\}.$$

**Dimension.** The set $\{\lambda I : \lambda \in \mathbb{C}\}$ is a one-dimensional subspace of $M_n(\mathbb{C})$, spanned by the single matrix $I$.

$$\boxed{\dim U_\perp = 1}$$
